cycles.name: Foundation Forge
focuses: Groove the hip-dominant glute and posterior-shoulder patterns and build a posture base.
Establish a recovery rhythm and a strong mind-muscle connection in the delts and glutes.

paragraphs: This first block isn't about chasing big numbers — it's about building the platform everything else stands on. Your job right now is to own the hip-hinge and shoulder patterns, wake up the glutes and rear delts that drive both your shape and your posture, and get your recovery working for you.

Mentally, chase the feeling, not the load: every rep at the prescribed tempo, every squeeze felt exactly where it should be. By the end of five weeks you'll move cleaner, stand taller, feel your delts and glutes switch on the way they should — and you'll have laid the foundation for the visible change that starts in Cycle 2.
outcomes: Cleaner, more controlled hip-hinge and pressing patterns
Glutes and rear delts that switch on when they should — real mind-muscle connection
Better posture — shoulders sitting back, ribs and pelvis stacked
A recovery rhythm that works for you: steadier sleep quality and protected rest days
Confident tempo and RPE control on every main lift
A foundation set for the visible change that starts in Cycle 2

cycles.name: Growth Engine
focuses: Drive shoulder and glute hypertrophy with added volume and reps taken closer to failure.
Progressively load the supported primaries — press, hip thrust, hack squat.

paragraphs: Cycle 1 was about learning the patterns. This one is about making them show. Your shoulders and glutes get genuinely loaded now — more sets, taken closer to failure, on the lifts you've already proven you can drive.

The big change is shape. Shoulders used to live on two days; now they're on all four. They were the thing you asked for and the thing your logs said was most under-trained, so they're no longer stuck on the days that are easiest to skip.

Week one sits close to where Cycle 1 finished — you've had time away and we're re-entering, not restarting. From week two the volume climbs. Hit the RPE on the card, log every set the same way, and this is the block where the mirror starts agreeing with the work.
outcomes: Rounder, wider-looking delts — the shape you came here for
A heavier hip thrust, and a hinge you can finally load without grinding
Shoulders trained four days a week instead of two
A back and rear delts strong enough to hold your posture without thinking about it
Core work you can actually feel, done where it belongs — at the end
A clean, readable log that shows exactly how much stronger you got

cycles.name: Metabolic Shift
focuses: Strip body fat while preserving the muscle already built to sharpen overall shape.
Hold training intensity in a deficit with strategic low-impact conditioning and steps.

paragraphs: Cycle 3 turns the focus to definition. Once the muscle is on, we bring the body fat down around it — training intensity held, steps and low-impact conditioning doing the fat-loss work, so everything you build now actually becomes visible.
Build it first. Then we reveal it.

cycles.name: Strength Engine
focuses: Intensify load on the primary lifts to raise the strength ceiling that future growth sits on.
Reinforce posture and bracing under heavier loads.

cycles.name: Sculpt & Define
focuses: A specialised shoulder-cap and glute-shaping block to maximise the target aesthetic.
Lock in balanced 3-D delt development and the corrected posture.

days.completionMessage: Heaviest upper day of the week and the delts led it — that's the session that changes your silhouette. Recover well.

good: Pull the band apart to touch your chest, arms straight
Feel the muscles between your shoulder blades draw together
bad: Don't let the traps shrug up toward your ears

good: Press your forearms into the wall and reach tall at the top
Feel the muscle along your ribs push the shoulder blades apart
bad: Don't arch the lower back to gain height

good: Elbow pinned to your ribs, rotate the forearm outward
Feel the back of the shoulder doing the turning
bad: Don't let the elbow drift away from your side

good: Move through the spine one segment at a time
Feel the mid-back opening on each round
bad: Don't rush the transitions

exercises.name: Machine Shoulder Press
exercises.note: You reset to the lightest setting when you came back on 25 July — start there for week one, then climb. Before your break you were pressing five plates, so there's ground to take back.

good: Press the handles in a smooth arc to just short of lockout
Feel the front and side delt driving, not the chest
bad: Letting the lower back arch off the pad as you press

good: Pull the bar to the top of your chest, elbows down and back
Feel the lats start the pull before the arms join in
bad: Leaning back and using momentum to finish the rep

exercises.name: Cable Lateral Raise
exercises.note: You ran this at 10 out of 10 on all three sets last cycle when I'd asked for 9. Drop the pin a plate or two — fifteen controlled reps beats twelve you have to throw.

good: Lead with the elbow out to shoulder height
Feel the side of the shoulder burn the whole way through
bad: Letting the cable yank your arm back down

good: Hinge over and open the arms out wide to shoulder height
Feel the back of the shoulders squeezing the weights apart
bad: Bending the elbows more as you tire to swing the weight up

good: Pull the rope toward your eyes, splitting the ends apart at the finish
Feel the rear delts and the muscles between the blades working
bad: Letting the elbows drop and turning it into a straight row

exercises.name: Machine Chest Press
exercises.note: New to your program — chest was missing, and Amir wants it back in the mix. Keep it light and controlled; this supports the shoulder work this cycle, it isn't the focus.

good: Press the handles together until your arms are extended
Feel the chest doing the pressing, not the shoulders rolling forward
bad: Letting the shoulders round forward at the top of the press

good: Curl the hips off the floor and bring the knees toward your chest
Feel the lower abs lift you — not the legs swinging
bad: Using momentum to kick the legs up

days.completionMessage: The heaviest thing you'll do all week is done, and it's the lift you're best at. Eat, sleep, come back for it.

good: Drive through the heels and push the knees out against the band
Feel the glutes squeeze hard at the top
bad: Don't push the hips up through the lower back

good: Stay in a quarter-squat and step wide against the band
Feel the outside of the hips working to hold the stance
bad: Don't let the knees cave inward

good: Rotate both knees to the floor on one side, then the other
Feel the hips freeing up through the rotation
bad: Don't force the range — move where it's comfortable

good: Drive the knee forward over the toes, heel glued down
Feel the stretch through the back of the ankle
bad: Don't let the heel lift off the floor

exercises.name: Barbell Hip Thrust
exercises.note: Your best lift by a distance — 10 kg to 30 kg in three sessions without the effort changing. Eight reps at RPE 9 should mean more weight on the bar than 30 kg, so build up to it and find the number.

good: Drive the hips up until torso and thighs make a straight line
Feel the glutes lock hard at the top, ribs down
bad: Overextending the lower back at the top

good: Descend until the thighs pass parallel, knees tracking over the toes
Feel the quads and glutes loading evenly through full depth
bad: Cutting the depth short or letting the heels lift

exercises.name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
exercises.note: This replaces the barbell version — you were stuck at 20 kg there and grinding it at 9s and 10s. Dumbbells sit closer to your legs and let you own the hinge, so start lighter than the barbell felt and let the stretch do the work.

good: Push the hips back, lowering the weights along your thighs
Feel a deep hamstring stretch before you drive the hips forward
bad: Rounding the back or letting the weights drift away from the legs

good: Curl the pad all the way to your glutes
Feel the hamstrings shorten hard at the top
bad: Lifting the hips off the pad to finish the rep

good: Extend to straight legs and pause at the top
Feel the quads squeeze hard at full extension
bad: Slamming the pad down or bouncing out of the bottom

good: Curl the ribs toward the hips, chin off the chest
Feel the abs shorten and squeeze at the top of each rep
bad: Pulling on your neck with your hands

days.completionMessage: Second shoulder session of the week, free weights this time — different angle, same target. Recover well.

good: In a plank, push the floor away and let the blades spread, then pinch them
Feel the shoulder blades gliding on the ribcage
bad: Don't bend the elbows — this is all shoulder blade

good: Move slowly through a full overhead arc, hands wide
Feel the front of the shoulders and chest opening
bad: Don't force the range if the shoulder pinches

good: Hand behind the head, rotate the elbow up toward the ceiling
Feel the rotation coming from the mid-back
bad: Don't twist from the lower back

good: Arms straight, pull the band apart to your chest
Feel the shoulder blades draw together
bad: Don't shrug the traps up

exercises.name: Seated Dumbbell Overhead Press
exercises.note: New movement, and it takes the slot the barbell chest press used to have — pressing overhead serves your shoulders far better than pressing forward does. Start deliberately light; your first set tells you where to sit.

good: Press the dumbbells straight overhead until the arms are nearly locked
Feel the front and side delts drive the weight up
bad: Letting the ribs flare and the lower back arch

good: Row toward your waist, squeezing the shoulder blades together
Feel the mid-back and rear delts pulling, chest glued to the pad
bad: Lifting the chest off the pad to gain leverage

exercises.name: Dumbbell Lateral Raise
exercises.note: You tried 5 kg last cycle and the reps fell apart. Go back to a lighter dumbbell and hold every rep honest for all fifteen — this one grows on control, not weight.

good: Lead with the elbows to shoulder height, little finger edge slightly up
Keep the side delt under tension the whole set — no rest at the bottom
bad: Swinging or shrugging to throw the weight up

good: Open the arms out and back in a wide arc to shoulder height
Feel the rear delts squeezing the handles apart
bad: Bending the elbows more through the set to cheat the weight

exercises.name: Leaning Cable Lateral Raise
exercises.note: New setup — grab the low pulley with the far hand (crossing your body), lean away from the machine so your arm hangs across you, then raise it out and up. The lean is what makes this different from your usual raise: it keeps the cable pulling on the shoulder all the way to the top, instead of going slack there.

good: Lean away from the machine and raise the handle out and up past shoulder height
Feel the side delt stay under tension even at the very top of the raise
bad: Standing upright — that lets the cable go slack and turns it into a normal raise

good: Lie back on the incline and curl with the elbows behind your body
Feel the biceps stretch at the bottom before they shorten
bad: Swinging the elbows forward to start the rep

exercises.name: Hanging Knee Raise
exercises.note: If your grip gives out before your abs do, use the elbow supports on the captain's chair, or swap in reverse crunches for the day — the point is twelve reps you feel in the lower abs, not the hang itself.

good: Hang tall, then curl the knees up toward your chest
Feel the lower abs rolling the hips up underneath you
bad: Swinging the legs instead of lifting them

days.completionMessage: Single-leg work, side glutes and a last hit on the delts — the quiet session that keeps everything balanced. Rest up.

good: Heels together, open the knees against the band
Feel the outside of the hip switch on
bad: Don't roll the pelvis backward

good: Quarter-squat, step wide and keep the band tight
Feel the side glutes holding the stance
bad: Don't let the knees cave

good: Hinge over on one leg and rotate the hips open, then closed
Feel the standing hip working to keep you steady
bad: Don't rush it — stay braced and balanced

good: Lunge deep, drop the elbow inside the foot, then rotate open
Feel the hip flexor and mid-back opening together
bad: Don't let the back knee slam into the floor

exercises.name: Dumbbell Split Squat
exercises.note: A deliberate step down from the Bulgarian version — both feet stay on the floor now. You were grinding that one at 9s and 10s with the reps falling off; this one you can actually load and build on.

good: Drop straight down until the back knee nearly touches the floor
Feel the front-leg glute stretch and drive you back up
bad: Letting the front knee cave in or pushing off the back foot

exercises.name: Machine Leg Press
exercises.note: New machine for you — set the seat so the knees track over the toes, and stop the descent just before your lower back lifts off the pad. Your first set finds the working weight.

good: Push the platform away until the legs are nearly straight, knees soft at the top
Feel the quads and glutes load evenly through the whole range
bad: Locking the knees out hard or letting them cave inward

exercises.name: 45° Back Extension
exercises.note: You did this with bodyweight last cycle and it was already at RPE 8-9 by the third set — hold a plate against your chest this time so it keeps earning its place.

good: Rise to a straight line and squeeze the glutes at the top
Feel the glutes and hamstrings driving, not the lower back
bad: Hyperextending the lower back past neutral at the top

good: Curl the pad down and under, hips pinned to the seat
Feel the hamstrings shorten hard at the bottom
bad: Letting the hips rise off the seat to finish the rep

exercises.name: Cable Hip Abduction
exercises.note: You held this at the same setting all last cycle and only ever rated it 8 when I'd asked for 9 — there's a plate or two of headroom sitting unused here.

good: Lift the leg out to the side, torso upright
Feel the upper outer glute working, brief squeeze at the top
bad: Leaning away or swinging the leg with momentum

good: Curl up one vertebra at a time, then lower with control
Feel the abs doing the work through the whole range
bad: Throwing the arms forward to get up

cards.title: Thirty Kilos Says This Works
cards.body:
Your hip thrust went from 10 kg to 30 kg in three sessions — and the effort never changed. Same RPE 8, same clean reps, triple the load.

That's not a small thing. That's your body proving it responds to training, in writing, in your own log. It's also why the hip thrust stays the anchor of Day 2 and why the reps drop to eight while the effort goes up. You've earned heavier.

cards.title: Two Full Days On Your Shoulders
cards.body:
You asked for more shoulder work, and your logs agreed with you — last cycle your delts got trained about a third as much as your glutes did.

So Day 1 and Day 3 are both shoulder days now, and they come at the muscle from different angles rather than just piling more sets onto one movement:

  • Day 1 — machine pressing, your cable lateral raise, rear-delt work, a face pull, and a light chest movement
  • Day 3 — pressing overhead with dumbbells, a lateral raise, a rear-delt movement, and a new cable raise that keeps tension on the shoulder all the way to the top of the movement

Side-delt and rear-delt volume are both up sharply, the pressing has doubled, and — since it went missing entirely last cycle — chest is back in the program. And Day 1 is the session you never miss, so the muscle you care about most now sits on the day you're most likely to train.

cards.title: What Your Blood Test Said
cards.body:
I read your results. Most of it came back genuinely good — your iron, thyroid, B12 and blood sugar are all where I'd want them. Whatever's been making you feel flat, it isn't your blood work falling apart.

One thing did stand out: your vitamin D came back low. That's worth taking seriously, because low vitamin D tracks with exactly what you've been logging — poor sleep quality even after a long night, and energy that never quite arrives. A hard few months will do that on its own too; this just means there's something concrete you can fix alongside it.

This one is your doctor's call, not mine. Take the results back to her and ask specifically about the vitamin D. If it gets corrected, the sleep and energy scores you log should start moving — and everything downstream of them will too.

cards.title: Core Moved To The End
cards.body:
You told me you want your core work at the end of the session, and that you want to actually feel it. Both done.

Core is now the last block of every day, and the anti-rotation work is gone. In its place: crunches, reverse crunches, knee raises and sit-ups — movements where the contraction is obvious and you know you've worked.

Treat them like everything else here: slow down, respect the tempo, make the reps hard rather than fast.

cards.title: The RPE Is The Instruction
cards.body:
Two things in your logs to tidy up, and both are quick.

The RPE number is an instruction, not a score. Last cycle your lateral raises ran at 10 out of 10 when the card said 9, and your abduction work ran at 8 when the card said 9 — too heavy on one, too light on the other. Pick the load that lands you on the number written on the card. Easier than the target, go up. Grinding past it, come down.

Log the same way every time. Last cycle I saw 20.10, 00..10, 25 and 15.2 all in the same file, and I couldn't always tell the weight from the reps. Put the weight in the weight box and the reps in the reps box, every set — then I can actually see your progress instead of guessing at it.

cards.title: A Short Session Still Counts
cards.body:
Last cycle had a month in it where training stopped. You've told me why, and I'm not going to treat a stretch like that as a discipline problem — it wasn't. But I'd rather build the plan so it survives the next hard week than hope there won't be one.

So here's what you're allowed to do, officially:

  • Any order. The four days don't have to run 1-2-3-4. Do whichever one fits the day you're having.
  • Short on time? The warm-up plus the first two exercises is a real session. Log it and go home — that's not half a workout, that's the workout.
  • Rough day? Drop every RPE on the card by one and train lighter. Turning up light beats not turning up.
  • Two days instead of four? Still a training week. Day 1 is your shoulder day and Day 2 is your glute day — those two on their own cover both of your goals.

The one thing I'd ask: if you know you're going to be off for a while, send me a message. I can shrink the plan to two days a week, or park it properly until you're ready — so you come back to something that fits, instead of something you feel behind on.

cards.title: When To Stop A Set
cards.body:
Nothing in your program is restricted, and your bloods were reassuring on that front. But you're the one in the room, so here's the line.

Normal and fine: muscles burning, feeling tired, being stiff the next day. Train through all of it.

Not fine: sharp pain, anything that radiates, numbness or tingling, or pain low in the abdomen or hip that builds through a set instead of staying flat.

  • Mild and fading — finish the set, tell me afterwards
  • Building, or changing how you move — stop that exercise, use another for the slot, message me
  • Sharp, radiating, numb, or just unfamiliar — stop the session, message me before the next one

This matters most on the hip thrust, the dumbbell Romanian deadlift and the deeper hip work. I'd always rather hear about it early than find out a month later.
